title: Adaptive capacitor for committed throughput SLAs
creator: Priya Kapoor
description: Problem: Dedicated customers purchasing committed throughput are experiencing SLA breaches during bursty, correlated traffic spikes because our reactive autoscaler ramps too slowly and sometimes overshoots during recovery. Goal: design and implement an 'adaptive capacitor' autoscaling component that reserves short-term headroom, enforces conservative ramp rates, and supports graceful fallback policies so committed throughput SLAs are met while avoiding destabilizing fleet oscillation and runaway cost exposure. This ticket covers: target metric selection (sustained QPS windows, p99 latency for tail-sensitive models, token/sec output), scaling algorithm design (reservoir-based headroom, leaky-bucket drain, derivative-limited PID with hysteresis), safety limits (max ramp multiplier, cooldown windows, emergency fallback), simulation harness and unit/integration tests, console controls and observability, rollout plan with canary phases and runbook updates.
acceptance_criteria: Simulation harness demonstrates <1.5% SLA breach rate on our 10 synthetic burst patterns using historical tenant traces
Max scale-up multiplier limited to 2.5x within any 10-minute window unless emergency flag enabled
Cooldown period of at least 3 minutes after any scale event for the same tenant group unless overridden by operator
Fallback policy to compatible lower-cost model variant or degraded QPS path executes within 30s of sustained headroom starvation and generates an auditable event
Console exposes knobs: committed-reservation, surge-bank-size, max-ramp-multiplier, emergency-override and shows predicted headroom given current demand
notes: 2026-02-16: Kickoff — scoped algorithm variants (reservoir, PID, and rule-based hybrid). Agreed to prototype reservoir + derivative limiter.
2026-02-21: Data analysis — looked at 18 months of dedicated tenant traces; 7% of tenants exhibit >4x short bursts lasting 30s-5min. These are often due to batched user backfills.

2026-03-01: Design review PT1 — Product asked for explicit billing implications; decided to tag surge usage for reconciliation rather than immediate metering to avoid surprises. Action: Billing integration ticket follow-up.

2026-03-04: Engineering decision — implement leaky-bucket drain to smooth short spikes, and attach a small guaranteed reservation computed from 95th percentile of sustained 5-minute windows per tenant.

2026-03-08: Prototype tests — local sim shows reduced oscillation vs current reactive autoscaler, but underestimates recovery time when many tenants surge simultaneously. Added global surge-bank cap to prevent fleet-wide thrash.
2026-03-09: PR opened for runtime changes (see attachment). Seeking review from @Ava Thompson (Runtime), @Luca Chen (SRE).
2026-03-10: Security review kickoff scheduled; scope limited to control-plane gating and audit logs. Security requested explicit threat model for emergency-override path.

Next steps: finish simulator edge cases for correlated tenant bursts, implement dashboard telemetry for new metrics, add e2e canary in dedicated-us-east region, update runbooks and playbooks for incident response.
